The method is `detect_binary`, defined on `Core` in `crates/searcher/src/searcher/core.rs` (line 215).

It takes a buffer and a range. It pulls the configured marker byte out of `BinaryDetection::Quit(b)` or `BinaryDetection::Convert(b)`, then looks for that byte in `buf[range]` with `find_byte`. If it finds one, it records `binary_byte_offset` and reports it through the sink's `binary_data`. It returns `true` to stop the search when the sink says to stop. Otherwise it returns `true` only when the mode is `Quit`, so in `Convert` mode scanning continues.

The method is `detect_binary`, defined in `crates/searcher/src/searcher/core.rs` at line 215.

It takes a buffer and a range within it. It looks up the single configured binary byte, which comes from either `BinaryDetection::Quit(b)` or `BinaryDetection::Convert(b)`. It then searches that range for the byte with `find_byte`. If it finds one, it records `binary_byte_offset` and calls `binary_data`. It returns `true` (stop searching this file) if `binary_data` says to stop, or if the mode is `Quit`. In `Convert` mode it returns `false` so scanning continues.
